description.html: The decorative root looks like old wood bleached by water and sun. It is low and branching, with arms reaching out in all directions, and its furrowed surface is dotted with many holes. A hollow, stump-like part rises in the middle, with openings on top and on the side, giving the root a natural, wild look.

In an aquarium, the holes and the space under the arms serve as a hide for fish and shrimp, and the root nicely frames plants and stones. In a terrarium, lizards and snakes use it for climbing, for rubbing against during shedding and for hiding in the hollow part. Thanks to its low shape, it suits the foreground and midground, where it is most visible.

Before placing the root, rinse it well with lukewarm water and brush it, without detergent. Position it so it sits firmly on the bottom and does not wobble; in a terrarium, check that the animal cannot get stuck in any of the narrow holes. During regular cleaning, take the root out, rinse it and remove dirt from the hollows with a soft brush.
